overview_raw: The Technical Arts Advanced Diploma is a 12-month full-time program led by industry professionals. Students gain hands-on skills to conceptualize and execute visual effects, game development, and animation projects. As technical artists, they integrate artistic vision with technical expertise to enhance and streamline the production process. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. BCIT programs respond to the evolving needs of industry. Please note this program is currently undergoing a review that may result in changes to the curriculum. For more information or updates, please contact Mike Monks . Delivery: blended. See details . With BCIT’s Advanced Diploma in Technical Arts, you will develop the skills to become a creative problem solver, who can visualize and deliver solutions that bridge the technical and content side of visual effects, game, and animation projects. Technical Artists are in high demand in the digital entertainment and interactive media industry for their ability to integrate and synthesize the artistic vision and technical aspects of projects. They collaborate with artists and programmers to set up and maintain the art production workflow, and identify and develop tools to improve, troubleshoot and streamline the production process. About the program Employers value BCIT’s applied, job-ready approach to education and years of experience training students for success in the digital arts sector. 1 year to complete – start your technical arts career in 12 months Weekend and blended course delivery – earn an advanced level credential while you continue working Cohort delivery – build a professional network that will last long after you graduate Hands-on, applied courses – develop and refine your technical art and scripting skills Project sequence – complete a series of team projects that reflect the day-to-day work environment of a Technical Artist Industry instructors – learn from industry professionals with real-world experience in technical arts Learn more about program goals and how this program prepares you for a career in technical arts on the Program Details page. Who should apply for the Advanced Diploma in Technical Arts? This program is right for you if: You want a career that combines creativity and imagination with technical expertise. You are a programmer with a creative bent, or an artist with an affinity for logic and detail, ready to launch a new career in an exciting field. You are already working in the digital entertainment industry and want to expand your skillset and capitalize on growing job opportunities in this emerging area. You hold a diploma, degree or equivalent credential, or have a minimum of 5 years work experience in a related field, such as gaming, animation, film, TV, visual effects or programming, and have completed some post-secondary coursework. You are well organized and enjoy collaborating with others and working in teams. If this sounds like you, apply today on the Entry Requirements page, where you will also learn more about entrance requirements for this program. What graduates can do Technical Artists work in a broad range of positions related to video game production, animation and visual effects for TV and film, and interactive experiences across all digital platforms, in small boutique studios through to large multinational companies. Learn more about career opportunities awaiting you on the Graduating and Jobs page. Industry support BCIT’s Advanced Diploma in Technical Arts was developed with extensive industry input to provide you with the applied skills for success in this fast-growing field, including techniques, methodologies and scripting to create production and shading tools, procedural operations and assets for game, film and animation projects. entrance_requirements_raw: Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted during the following periods: Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intake may fill before the deadline. Entrance requirements This program has a two-step admission process. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis after department review as long as space remains. Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma or degree (or equivalent post-secondary program of a minimum of 60 credits) in any discipline or alternate entry* Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the selection for this program. Submit a portfolio of your creative artwork with your online application: Submit your digital portfolio highlighting expertise in artistic or technical fields, featuring the applicant’s best work in 3D art, animation, visual effects, game design, or programming for web, mobile, game, and desktop applications. A portfolio or link to your portfolio must be submitted at the time you apply for the program. Your application will not be processed until all required documents are submitted, so ensure your portfolio is ready before you start your application. Alternate entry: If you do not meet the post-secondary education requirement listed above, you may qualify for admission if you meet the English requirement, and the following: Post-secondary education: 30.0 credits in any discipline from a recognized institution Work experience: 5 years in a related field or sector such as gaming, animation, film, visual effects, or computer programming, in one of the following roles (or similar): Animator Effects artist Lighting artist Character modeling Props modeling Game level artist Game designer Game developer Producer UI/UX designer Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Self-Assessment [PDF] Contact the Program Head to discuss your particular situation. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a basic evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . A comprehensive report may be required under certain circumstances. If you wish to clarify which report is required, please contact digitalarts@bcit.ca . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Department assessment In order to be accepted to this program, all applications will be reviewed by the program area. Recommended for success Applicants are strongly encouraged to attend an information session before applying to this program. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : This program currently meets the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. ( CIPC : 9.0702) Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. program_details_raw: The Advanced Diploma in Technical Arts program was developed with the support and collaboration of Electronic Arts, Sony Pictures Imageworks, and The Coalition. This program is an Unreal Engine Academic Partner . Program goals Upon successful completion of the Advanced Diploma in Technical Arts, you will be able to: Design and creation Design and develop tools for 3D modeling, texturing, and animation. Create procedural shaders for 3D applications and game engines. Create animator-friendly rigs for 3D models. Perform visual scripting in game engines to automate and enhance the asset pipeline. Produce an industry standard project (animation, tools, rigs, and game). Apply a broad range of software techniques and methodologies used by studios. Project management Plan, design, troubleshoot and carry out a technical art project, from start to finish, with well-defined objectives. Track project deliverables and ensure that milestones are met. Streamline processes at different stages of art production. Communicate effectively with all stakeholders and departments to clarify and advise on goals and actions pertaining to visual effects, animation or game projects. Communication and teamwork Demonstrate effective teamwork and problem-solving skills. Demonstrate a professional work ethic. Use effective communication strategies for presenting technical arts project proposals related to, for example, development of tools, user interfaces, and assets. Program length One year cohort program, delivered over 12 consecutive months, on weekends (Saturdays and Sundays) with some blended course delivery. All program requirements must be completed within three years. Program delivery Blended: This program is delivered partly on campus and partly online. The program is a 15-course advanced diploma delivered in a cohort model over three, 15-week terms. Once you are accepted in to the program, you will complete all 15 courses with your cohort. Each of the three, 15-week terms is split into two equal parts — Part A and Part B — with two courses completed in Part A (over seven weeks, in a computer lab) and two courses completed in Part B (over seven weeks, in a computer lab). In addition, one project-related course will be delivered each term in a blended delivery mode over the full term (15 weeks). Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Distance and online learning Go back Courses Next up Graduating & Jobs

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course will cover the fundamentals of computer programming and the logic behind it. Students will learn the essentials of programming and basic scripting for 3D applications, including variables, arrays, different types of loops, conditions and functions. The cousre also introduces students to Python, a standard scripting language used in a variety of technical art fields. Python is used in the production process for scripting complex computer graphic intensive films, animation and 3D tools. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Understanding the 3D environment is fundamental for technical artists. This course will cover the basics of 3D applications, animation, materials, and scripting, as well as polygon modeling techniques for simple 3D objects. The course will introduce students to Maya ® , one of the most popular 3D applications used by the visual effects, animation, and game industries. Students will navigate different environments within the Maya ® application, becoming familiar with modeling menus, Hypershade, and render settings. Students will complete a series of 3D projects, creating basic objects, materials, character rigs, and scripts in a 3D environment.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

This course is the first of a three-course series for students to develop the core knowledge and skills of a technical artist in the visual effects, animation and game industries. In this first course in the series, students will be introduced to the role and activities of the technical artist in bridging the programming and artistic side of projects, such as streamlining assets and code or improving visual appeal. Students will learn the complete production pipeline, from the perspective of both the art and engineering side. Throughout this course, students will work under an instructor’s supervision on industry standard technical art projects and develop skills in rigging, technical applications, shader creation, physics, effects and particles. Prerequisite(s): TECA 5100

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course introduces students to project management tools and techniques in the context of technical arts, and prepares students for a series of team project courses in Terms 2 and 3. In this introductory project management course, students will learn the roles and responsibilities of technical artists and the unique characteristics of the production pipeline for visual effects, animation, and game projects. Students will learn fundamental project planning techniques such as agile or waterfall methdologies. We will discuss the common sources of difficulty in project management, such as communication issues, people management, and project control using check points and milestones. Students will also use project management software to practice their project management skills and become familiar with common software aids. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

This course focuses on creating and developing procedures and functions inside industry standard 3D applications and game engines using visual scripting methodology. Students will learn the fundamentals of visual scripting in several 3D applications and game engines through the creation of materials, blueprints, effects, dynamics and event controls. Topics also include creating events and triggers (including collision-based events), developing loops and conditions to execute functions, and performing the required mathematical calculations. Prerequisite(s): TECA 5000

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: This course looks at different art assets used in the production and development of a video game. Students will be introduced to standard game engines used in game studios. While exploring the game engine and its different panels and environments, students will be taught the dos and don’ts of creating 3D game models, lighting, textures, and shaders. Students will create a small game level using 3D assets, audio, and textures; visual scripting; and lights, camera, environment effects, and dynamics. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

In this course, students will build on their programming and scripting skills within industry standard 3D applications. Programming with Python, students will apply standard coding practices used by technical artists in developing expressions, user interfaces, tools, and functions. In addition, students will learn the essential elements of user-centric design and user experience. ​ Prerequisite(s): TECA 5100

Building on knowledge and skills developed in Technical Arts 1, this course will focus on creating 3D-friendly shaders and materials for different projects used in the visual effects, animation, and game industries. In this course, students will use industry standard applications to develop materials and visual effects. In addition, students will create and optimize textures to be imported into 3D applications and game engines ​ Prerequisite(s): TECA 5200

In this course students develop object-oriented scripts with Python. The focus is on problem-solving in scripts, proper object-oriented programming (OOP) techniques, and clear coding style. The fundamental principles of OOP (data abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism) are covered with emphasis on inheritance and polymorphism. Students will examine data structures such as linked lists, queues, stacks, trees and common search and sort algorithms. Students will also explore scripting in more depth, creating interfaces, tools, exception handling and user interfaces in Python. Prerequisite(s): TECA 6300

This course is the first of two courses in the team project sequence. The goal of the team project sequence is to prepare students for the deadline-oriented, results-driven, team-based environment that technical artists work in. Students will have the opportunity to use project management skills developed in Term 1. Students will be placed in teams to pitch, prototype, and deliver a technical art project, such as developing and optimizing tools, dynamic assets, procedural shaders and/or textures. Students will experiment with scripting, user interfaces and modeling techniques, and will apply technical and artistic skills specific to the project they are completing. Each week teams will discuss their progress with their instructor and receive feedback through team meetings and online sessions. The instructor will sign off on each milestone as the teams present their work. Prerequisite(s): TECA 5600

This course introduces the concept of dynamics in 3D applications. Students will learn the fundamentals of physics and the essentials of several dynamic elements, such as rigid bodies, cloth, hair, particles, and pyro. Students will create different dynamic objects and experiment with various environmental elements and their effect on objects. An important component of this course is completion of various projects related to dynamic elements and environment, which contribute to students’ individual portfolios. ​ Prerequisite(s): TECA 5300

This course builds on Technical Arts 2, where students developed their skills in designing shaders, procedural materials, and textures. In Technical Arts 3, students focus on advanced technical procedures and camera setup to light and render scenes in 3D applications and game engines. They will create expressions and develop scripts for dynamic lighting, camera movement, and effects. Finally, students will learn advanced rendering techniques: managing and prioritizing data, troubleshooting and optimizing materials, and ensuring the smooth operation of rendering processes. ​ Prerequisite(s): TECA 6100

This course focuses on advanced object-oriented programming techniques in Python. It builds on the skills developed with scripting and data structures. Students will create and develop scripts and expressions that control node attributes within 3D applications and that connect nodes to influence one another. In addition, students will create and implement pre- and post-render scripting options to automate time-consuming processes. Students will also develop tools that provide flexibility and ease of modeling, texturing, shading, rigging, animation, and rendering processes throughout different stages of the production pipeline. ​ Prerequisite(s): TECA 5400

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: Effective teamwork skills are essential to success as a technical artist, as a core member of the production team, or as the team lead. Developing a strong team and improving team performance leads to better project outcomes. Students will participate in the various stages of team development and learn decision-making and conflict resolution techniques, as well as how to solve problems and collaborate effectively with others. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

In this second of two courses in the team project sequence, students will have further opportunity to experience the types of projects that reflect a technical artist’s day-to-day work environment. They will propose ideas for projects related to visual effects, animation, or games, which should be tools related to dynamics, user interfaces, animation, and/or modeling. Students will form interdisciplinary teams based on their skill sets and interests, and execute collaborative projects that turn their ideas into reality. Teams will plan, track, and troubleshoot each stage of the collaborative project. In this final team project course, students are expected to show advanced technical art and scripting skills. Each week teams will discuss their progress with their instructor and receive feedback through team meetings and online sessions. The instructor will sign off on each milestone as the teams present their work. At the end of the term, students’ must present their finished project to the instructor(s) and an industry panel. Prerequisite(s): TECA 6700
